name: gods-eye-view
description: A spy satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real. Live open source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe.
one_liner: A free, browser-based 'spy satellite' map that shows real live flights, ships, satellites, earthquakes, traffic, and public cameras on a photorealistic 3D globe you can talk to.
buyer: A news or media outlet, or a logistics/insurance team, that wants a live situational-awareness map for storytelling or risk monitoring without building satellite-data infrastructure from scratch.
business_use_cases: A news outlet embeds a live-tracked globe view in breaking-news coverage, following a specific flight or ship, instead of using static maps.
A logistics or insurance company builds an internal dashboard to monitor shipping lanes, weather, and asset locations in one view.
An explainer YouTube channel uses the scene director and cinematic camera tools to produce 'watch this unfold live' video segments for current events.

money_ideas.idea: White-label the globe as an embeddable live-event widget for news publishers, priced per embed.
Sell a managed hosted version with premium data feeds (higher-res imagery, more cameras) for logistics and insurance teams.

steal_this: A weekend 'live event tracker' page: point a hosted instance at a real unfolding event (storm, flight, ship) and share the link for traffic and ad revenue.
